Base-table ownership, as data. This file is the single enforcement source consumed by the hgcrossmodule analyzer (ADR-0039 D1: a module emitting raw SQL against a table another module owns is a violation). It replaces the hand-maintained Go map that used to live in hgcrossmodule.go, where an ownership fact could go stale silently — and did: governance_events was recorded as approval-owned because approval writes it, contradicting ADR 0044, which keeps it audit-owned. That single stale entry hid two foreign writes from the A4.0 census.

This file is NOT a second truth. table_ownership_parity_test.go asserts, on every `go test ./...`, that each entry agrees with the governed documentation in wiki/database/tables/<table>.md ('> **Owner:** <module>') after alias normalisation. A doc and this file disagreeing is a red build, not a judgement call. Where the governed doc labels a table with something that is not a module directory under internal/modules/ (platform-layer owners), the entry must acknowledge that label verbatim in wiki_owner — an explicit, reviewable divergence rather than a silent one.

Owner values are the top-level directory name under internal/modules/. 'Top-level' matters: iam/presence is inside iam, so a read across sub-packages of one module is not cross-module.

tables.note: approval's signature-reauth limiter; the governed doc agrees despite the auth_ prefix.

ADR 0044: the domain-event sink is audit-owned. approval INSERTs into it and iam DELETEs from it; both are foreign writes, and recording the writer as the owner (the pre-B4 state) made them invisible to the A4.0 census.
The governed doc labels this a platform concern rather than a module; enforcement needs a module directory, and internal/modules/jobs is where the store lives.
The governed doc labels the whole outbox/worker family platform/workers; the notifications module owns this table's writes.
